acne.description: Acne is a skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become clogged with oil and dead skin cells.
skincare: Use a salicylic acid (2%) face wash twice daily
Apply benzoyl peroxide spot treatment at night
Use a non-comedogenic oil-free moisturizer
Apply niacinamide serum to reduce inflammation
Always use SPF 30+ sunscreen daily
Never pop or squeeze pimples
food: Eat more fruits and vegetables (antioxidants)
Drink 8-10 glasses of water daily
Reduce dairy and high-glycemic foods
Include omega-3 rich foods (fish, walnuts, flaxseed)
Avoid sugary drinks and processed foods
Add zinc-rich foods (pumpkin seeds, chickpeas)
tips: Change pillowcases every 2-3 days
Avoid touching your face throughout the day
Clean phone screen with antibacterial wipe daily
Use clean makeup brushes and tools
Remove makeup thoroughly before sleeping
Manage stress with yoga or meditation
If it gets worse or doesn't improve in 4-6 weeks, see a dermatologist

darkcircles.description: Dark circles under the eyes are common and can be caused by fatigue, genetics, aging, or dehydration.
skincare: Apply a caffeine-based eye cream morning and night
Use vitamin K and retinol eye cream at night
Apply cold cucumber slices or tea bags for 10 minutes
Gently massage the under-eye area with aloe vera gel
Use a brightening vitamin C serum around eyes
Apply sunscreen around the eye area
food: Eat almonds, walnuts and vitamin E rich foods
Include iron-rich foods (spinach, lentils, red meat)
Drink plenty of water to reduce puffiness
Eat vitamin C rich citrus fruits
Reduce sodium intake to decrease water retention
Add collagen-boosting foods (bone broth, berries)
tips: Sleep 7-9 hours every night consistently
Elevate your head with an extra pillow
Limit alcohol and caffeine consumption
Wear UV-protective sunglasses outdoors
Use cool compresses to reduce puffiness
Try facial yoga and lymphatic drainage massage
If it gets worse or doesn't improve in 4-6 weeks, see a dermatologist

dry.description: Dry skin lacks moisture and natural oils, leading to flakiness, itching, and a dull complexion.
skincare: Use a gentle hydrating cleanser (no SLS/SLES)
Apply hyaluronic acid serum on damp skin
Use a thick ceramide-based moisturizer twice daily
Apply facial oil (rosehip, jojoba) as the last step
Use a sleeping mask 2-3 times per week
Exfoliate gently with lactic acid 1x per week
food: Eat avocados for healthy skin fats
Include fatty fish (salmon, mackerel) for omega-3
Drink at least 2 liters of water daily
Eat sweet potatoes rich in beta-carotene
Add nuts and seeds for vitamin E
Include olive oil in your diet
tips: Use a humidifier in your bedroom while sleeping
Take shorter, lukewarm (not hot) showers
Pat skin dry gently - never rub
Apply moisturizer within 3 minutes of washing
Wear gloves in cold or dry weather
Avoid alcohol-based and fragrance-heavy products
If it gets worse or doesn't improve in 4-6 weeks, see a dermatologist
products: First Aid Beauty Ultra Repair Cream

oily.description: Oily skin produces excess sebum, leading to a shiny appearance and increased risk of clogged pores.
skincare: Use a gentle gel or foam cleanser twice daily
Apply an alcohol-free toner with witch hazel
Use a lightweight oil-free gel moisturizer
Apply niacinamide serum to control oil production
Use clay or salicylic acid masks 1-2 times per week
Always use oil-free, non-comedogenic SPF
food: Avoid fried and greasy fast foods
Reduce refined carbohydrates and sugar
Drink 8+ glasses of water daily
Eat green leafy vegetables for antioxidants
Include zinc-rich foods to regulate sebum
Reduce dairy consumption if acne-prone
tips: Use blotting papers throughout the day
Wash your face no more than twice daily
Avoid over-moisturizing or skipping moisturizer
Use oil-free, water-based makeup products
Clean makeup brushes regularly
Do not skip sunscreen - use oil-free formulas
If it gets worse or doesn't improve in 4-6 weeks, see a dermatologist
products: La Roche-Posay Effaclar Purifying Foaming Gel

normal.description: Normal skin is well balanced: not too oily, not too dry, with few visible concerns.
skincare: Use a gentle cleanser twice daily
Apply a light moisturizer morning and night
Use SPF 30+ sunscreen every day
Add a vitamin C serum in the morning for glow
Exfoliate gently 1-2 times per week
Remove makeup before sleeping
food: Eat a balanced diet with fruits and vegetables
Drink 8 glasses of water daily
Include omega-3 foods (fish, walnuts, flaxseed)
Add vitamin C rich foods (citrus, berries)
Limit sugary and processed foods
Eat nuts and seeds for vitamin E
tips: Sleep 7-8 hours every night
Avoid touching your face
Change pillowcases weekly
Do not over-wash or over-exfoliate
Manage stress with exercise or meditation
Keep your routine simple and consistent
If you notice new concerns that persist for 4-6 weeks, see a dermatologist
